h: Castles, Monuments and a Famous Film Location Nearby
p: Blair Drummond sits on the edge of the Carse of Stirling, the flat, fertile plain that runs west from the city along the River Forth, with the Highlands rising behind. It's a gorgeous spot, and you're very well placed to make a weekend of it.

Just a few minutes up the road, Doune Castle is a remarkably complete medieval castle that has had a busy screen career. It starred in Monty Python and the Holy Grail and was used as Castle Leoch in Outlander, as well as appearing in Game of Thrones. The audio tour leans into the film history, so even kids who aren't into old stones tend to enjoy it.

Head the other way and Stirling Castle looms over the city from its volcanic crag, with the National Wallace Monument perched on Abbey Craig across the valley. Climbing the monument's spiral stairs is a proper challenge for little legs, but the views over the Forth are worth every step. Nearby, the town of Doune itself is a pretty stop for a coffee, and Callander, the gateway to the Trossachs, is a short drive further on.

Practical tip: the park is a big day, so start early. Pack a cool bag, because once you're in the car on the drive-through, you won't want to stop for snacks. And keep an eye on the forecast. It's an outdoor attraction at heart, and Scottish weather can shift fast.
